intro: Hi! On Monday a colleague asks 'How was your weekend?', and on Friday 'What are you going to do this weekend?'. In this lesson you put the past simple and going to together and answer like in a real conversation: say what you did, add a detail, share your plans and ask back. Warm-up: how was your weekend?
teachingNotes: This is a speaking lesson: it practises grammar the learner already has (past simple, regular and irregular, with did questions; going to and the present continuous for fixed arrangements) inside conversation frames. Teach the frames as chunks: How was your weekend / holiday? — It was great / OK / not bad. What did you do? — I went to… / I stayed at home. What are you going to do this weekend? — I'm going to… What are you doing on Saturday? — I'm meeting… Practise them as a short chat, not as grammar drills.

The #1 error (the node's common error): Indonesian has no past form, only the time word (Minggu lalu saya pergi ke pantai), so learners say *'Last weekend I go to the beach with my family' → 'Last weekend I went to the beach with my family.' In a story, check EVERY verb, not just the first one (*'I went to Bogor and eat sate'), and 'It was great', not *'It's great', about a finished weekend. Also watch the mismatch between question and answer: a did question gets the past, a going to / are you doing question gets the future. *'I was go' (was + verb) is another common error.

Adding detail: who (with my family, with friends from work, on my own = sendirian), where (to Puncak, at a warung, in Bandung) and what it was like (It was + adjective: fun, delicious, crowded, relaxing, tiring, beautiful, expensive). Traps: 'seru' is fun, not funny (funny = lucu, makes you laugh); 'ramai' about a place is crowded; 'macet' is 'The traffic was terrible'. 'It was tiring' = the activity made you tired; 'I was tired' = you were tired (not *'It was tired'). Join ideas with and, but, because.

Follow-up questions: answer with the short answer AND one more fact (Did you have a good time? — Yes, I did! We saw the sunset. / Was it expensive? — No, it wasn't. It was only 50,000 rupiah.). A bare 'Yes' or 'Yes, I did' is correct but stops the chat. The short answer copies the first word of the question: Did → I did / I didn't; Was → it was / it wasn't. Watch *'Yes, I do' and *'Yes, I was' to a did question, and *'Yes, I saw' (English doesn't repeat the main verb in a short answer).

Asking back: And you? / How about you? / What about you? (from a1-everyday-conversation), or a real follow-up: Where did you go? What did you eat? Was it fun? Who did you go with? Word order is question word + did + person + base verb; watch *'Where you went?' and *'Where did you went?'. Indonesian 'sama siapa' at the end leads to *'With who you went?': in English 'with' goes at the end (Who did you go with?). Short reactions from A1 are welcome: Really? That's great! Oh no!

Plans: going to for your own plan, present continuous + a time for something fixed with other people; accept both for plans, but never the simple present (*'Tomorrow I go to Bogor' → 'Tomorrow I'm going to Bogor'). 'I'm going to Bali' (going to + a place) is the present continuous of go; 'I'm going to go to Bali' is also correct. Fixed answers when there's no plan: Nothing special. / I'm not sure. Limits: no will (a2-will), no present perfect (Have you ever…? I've been to…), no past continuous, no sequencing with first / then / so (a2-linkers-sequence), no invitations (a2-making-plans). British 'at the weekend' and 'holiday' vs American 'on the weekend' and 'vacation': both fine.

keyPoints.title: Tell about your weekend: It was… + past verbs + a detail
keyPoints.explanation: Answer How was your weekend? with It was + a word (great, OK, busy) or Not bad. Then say what you did with past verbs (went, ate, visited, stayed) and add a detail: who, where, or what it was like (It was fun / delicious / crowded). The weekend is finished, so every verb in your story is past: I went, not I go.

examples.en: How was your weekend? — It was great! I went to Bogor with my family.
examples.id: Akhir pekanmu gimana? — Seru! Saya ke Bogor sama keluarga.

examples.en: We ate sate at a warung. It was delicious.
examples.id: Kami makan sate di warung. Enak banget.

examples.en: It was OK. I stayed at home and cleaned the kitchen.
examples.id: Biasa aja. Saya di rumah dan membersihkan dapur.

id.title: Cerita akhir pekan: It was… + kata kerja lampau + detail
id.explanation: Jawab How was your weekend? dengan It was + satu kata (great, OK, busy) atau Not bad. Lalu ceritakan apa yang kamu lakukan dengan kata kerja bentuk lampau (went, ate, visited, stayed) dan tambahkan detail: dengan siapa, di mana, atau bagaimana rasanya (It was fun / delicious / crowded). Akhir pekannya sudah selesai, jadi semua kata kerja dalam ceritamu berbentuk lampau: I went, bukan I go.

keyPoints.title: Your plans: I'm going to… / I'm meeting… on Saturday
keyPoints.explanation: What are you going to do this weekend? → your own plan: I'm going to + verb. What are you doing on Saturday? → something fixed with other people: I'm + verb-ing + a time. No plans? Nothing special. / I'm not sure. Never the simple present for a plan: not 'Tomorrow I go to Bogor', but 'Tomorrow I'm going to Bogor'.

examples.en: What are you going to do this weekend? — I'm going to visit my aunt in Bekasi.
examples.id: Akhir pekan ini mau ngapain? — Saya mau mengunjungi tante di Bekasi.

examples.en: I'm meeting Sari at the cinema on Saturday at 7.
examples.id: Hari Sabtu jam 7 saya ketemu Sari di bioskop. (sudah janjian)

examples.en: Nothing special. I'm going to relax at home.
examples.id: Nggak ada yang spesial. Saya mau santai di rumah.

id.title: Rencanamu: I'm going to… / I'm meeting… on Saturday
id.explanation: What are you going to do this weekend? → rencanamu sendiri: I'm going to + kata kerja. What are you doing on Saturday? → acara yang sudah dijadwalkan dengan orang lain: I'm + kata kerja-ing + waktu. Belum ada rencana? Nothing special. / I'm not sure. Jangan pakai simple present untuk rencana: bukan 'Tomorrow I go to Bogor', tapi 'Tomorrow I'm going to Bogor'.

keyPoints.title: Follow-up questions: short answer + one more fact, then ask back
keyPoints.explanation: Answer a follow-up question with the short answer (Yes, I did. / No, it wasn't.) and one more fact, so the chat keeps going. The short answer copies the first word of the question: Did → I did, Was → it was. Then ask back: How about you? or a real question with did: Where did you go? Who did you go with?

examples.en: Did you have a good time? — Yes, I did! We saw the sunset from the hill.
examples.id: Seneng nggak? — Iya! Kami lihat matahari terbenam dari bukit.

examples.en: Was it expensive? — No, it wasn't. The hotel was only 300,000 rupiah a night.
examples.id: Mahal nggak? — Nggak. Hotelnya cuma 300.000 rupiah semalam.

examples.en: I went to Bandung. How about you? Where did you go?
examples.id: Saya ke Bandung. Kamu sendiri? Kamu ke mana?

id.title: Pertanyaan lanjutan: jawaban singkat + satu fakta lagi, lalu tanya balik
id.explanation: Jawab pertanyaan lanjutan dengan jawaban singkat (Yes, I did. / No, it wasn't.) dan satu fakta lagi, supaya obrolannya terus berjalan. Jawaban singkat mengikuti kata pertama pertanyaannya: Did → I did, Was → it was. Lalu tanya balik: How about you? atau pertanyaan sungguhan dengan did: Where did you go? Who did you go with?

guidedPractice.prompt: Correct the mistake: Last Saturday I eat bakso with my friends.

i ate bakso with my friends last saturday
guidedPractice.hint: Last Saturday is finished: what is the past of eat?

guidedPractice.prompt: Your friend asks: 'How was your weekend?' It was OK. Complete: It ___ OK. I stayed at home.
expected: was
guidedPractice.hint: The weekend is over: the past of is.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with going to + cook: This weekend I ___ for my parents.
expected: am going to cook
'm going to cook
m going to cook
guidedPractice.hint: am + going to + the plain verb.

guidedPractice.prompt: Dimas asks: 'Did you go out last night?' You didn't: you stayed at home. Answer with a short answer and one more fact.
expected: no i didn't i stayed at home
no i did not i stayed at home
no i didn't i stayed home
guidedPractice.hint: Did → I didn't. Then say what you did instead, in the past.

independentPractice.prompt: Tell a friend about your last holiday in two short sentences: where you went and what it was like.
expected: i went to bali it was beautiful
i went back to my hometown it was relaxing
i went to yogyakarta with my family it was fun
independentPractice.hint: I went to … + It was + a describing word (fun, beautiful, relaxing).

independentPractice.prompt: Your colleague asks: 'What are you doing on Sunday?' You're meeting your cousins at the mall (it's fixed). Answer.
expected: i'm meeting my cousins at the mall
i am meeting my cousins at the mall
i'm meeting my cousins at the mall on sunday
i am meeting my cousins at the mall on sunday
independentPractice.hint: Fixed with other people: I'm + verb-ing.

independentPractice.prompt: Rina says: 'I went to Malang last week.' Ask her one follow-up question.
expected: did you have a good time
what did you do there
who did you go with
was it fun
how was it
independentPractice.hint: Use did + the base verb, or Was it…?

assessment.prompt: On Monday Pak Hasan asks you: 'What did you do on Sunday?' Your Sunday: go to the mall with your sister. Answer in one sentence.
acceptableAnswers: i went to the mall with my sister
i went to the mall with my sister on sunday
on sunday i went to the mall with my sister
my sister and i went to the mall
i went to a mall with my sister
i went shopping at the mall with my sister
assessment.rubric: Correct: I went to the mall with my sister. 'I go to the mall…' = 30 (no past form: the Indonesian habit). 'I goed' = 40. 'I was go' = 30. Correct past but no 'with my sister' = 70 (the detail is missing). 'I'm going to go to the mall' = 0 (a plan, not what happened).

assessment.prompt: Listen to your colleague's question. Answer in one or two short sentences. Your facts: great · go to Lombok.
acceptableAnswers: it was great i went to lombok
it was great thanks i went to lombok
it was great thank you i went to lombok
great thanks i went to lombok
great i went to lombok
it was great we went to lombok
it was great i went to lombok with my family
assessment.rubric: Needs 'It was great' and 'I went to Lombok'. 'It's great' = 60 (the holiday is finished, so was). 'I go to Lombok' = 40 (no past). Only 'It was great' = 50 (Lombok is missing). 'I'm going to Lombok' = 0 (a plan).

assessment.prompt: It's Friday. Your friend asks: 'What are you going to do this weekend?' Your plan: clean your room. Answer with going to.
acceptableAnswers: i'm going to clean my room
i am going to clean my room
im going to clean my room
i'm going to clean my room this weekend
i am going to clean my room this weekend
this weekend i'm going to clean my room
this weekend i am going to clean my room
assessment.rubric: Correct: I'm going to clean my room. 'I going to clean' = 50 (am is missing). 'I'm going to cleaning / cleans' = 60 (after to, the plain verb). 'I clean my room' = 20 (sounds like a habit). 'I cleaned my room' = 0 (the past).

assessment.prompt: You're having dinner with Pak Hasan on Saturday: he booked a table for 7. Rina asks: 'What are you doing on Saturday?' Answer with the present continuous of 'have'.
acceptableAnswers: i'm having dinner with pak hasan
i am having dinner with pak hasan
im having dinner with pak hasan
i'm having dinner with pak hasan on saturday
i am having dinner with pak hasan on saturday
on saturday i'm having dinner with pak hasan
i'm having dinner with pak hasan at 7
i'm having dinner with pak hasan at seven
assessment.rubric: Correct: I'm having dinner with Pak Hasan. 'I'm going to have dinner with Pak Hasan' = 80 (correct English, but the task asks for the present continuous for a fixed plan). 'I having dinner' = 60 (am is missing). 'I have dinner with Pak Hasan' = 30 (sounds like a habit). 'I had dinner' = 0 (the past).

assessment.prompt: Sari asks: 'Did you have a good time at the beach?' Answer yes with a short answer, then add one detail. Your detail: take a lot of photos.
acceptableAnswers: yes i did i took a lot of photos
yes i did we took a lot of photos
yes i did i took lots of photos
yes i did and i took a lot of photos
yes i did i took a lot of pictures
yes i did i took many photos
assessment.rubric: Needs 'Yes, I did' + the detail in the past (I took a lot of photos). 'Yes, I do' = 50 (did question → did answer). Only 'Yes' or 'Yes, I did' = 50 (no detail). 'I take a lot of photos' = 60 (not past). 'I taked' = 70.

assessment.prompt: Your friend Dimas says: 'I went to Bali last month.' Ask him a follow-up question with Where and the verb 'stay'.
acceptableAnswers: where did you stay
where did you stay in bali
where did you stay there
dimas where did you stay
where did you stay dimas
assessment.rubric: Correct: Where did you stay? 'Where you stayed?' = 50 (no did: Indonesian word order). 'Where did you stayed?' = 60 (the past is shown twice: did already shows it). 'Where do you stay?' = 40 (present).

assessment.prompt: Listen to your friend. Answer her question in one sentence. Your weekend: stay at home and watch TV.
assessment.listen: I went to Bandung last weekend. How about you?
acceptableAnswers: i stayed at home and watched tv
i stayed home and watched tv
i just stayed at home and watched tv
i stayed at home and i watched tv
oh i stayed at home and watched tv
i stayed at home and watched tv last weekend
assessment.rubric: Correct: I stayed at home and watched TV. 'I stayed at home and watch TV' = 70 (both verbs need the past). 'I stay at home and watch TV' = 30 (no past). 'I'm going to stay at home' = 0 (a plan, but she asks about last weekend).

blocks.text:
Two questions you hear every Monday: **How was your weekend?** (= Akhir pekanmu gimana?) asks if it was good or bad, and **What did you do?** (= Kamu ngapain?) asks what happened.
- Answer the first with **It was** + a word: *It was great! / It was OK. / It was busy.* or **Not bad.** (*not bad* = lumayan, a good answer).
- Answer the second with **past verbs** you know: *I went to Bogor. I visited my grandma. I stayed at home.*

After a longer break, ask **How was your holiday?** (*holiday* is British; Americans say *vacation*). *At the weekend* is British and *on the weekend* American: both are fine.

id.text:
Dua pertanyaan yang kamu dengar setiap Senin: **How was your weekend?** (= Akhir pekanmu gimana?) menanyakan rasanya, dan **What did you do?** (= Kamu ngapain?) menanyakan apa yang terjadi.
- Jawab yang pertama dengan **It was** + satu kata: *It was great! / It was OK. / It was busy.* atau **Not bad.** (*not bad* = lumayan, jawaban yang baik).
- Jawab yang kedua dengan **kata kerja bentuk lampau** yang sudah kamu tahu: *I went to Bogor. I visited my grandma. I stayed at home.*

Setelah libur yang lebih panjang, tanya **How was your holiday?** (*holiday* itu British; orang Amerika bilang *vacation*). *At the weekend* itu British dan *on the weekend* Amerika: dua-duanya benar.

rows.en: How was your weekend? — It was great, thanks!
What did you do? — I went to Puncak.
It was OK. I stayed at home and cleaned the house.
rows.id: Biasa aja. Saya di rumah dan bersih-bersih rumah.

rows.en: How was your holiday? — Not bad. I went back to my hometown for Lebaran.
rows.id: Liburanmu gimana? — Lumayan. Saya mudik waktu Lebaran.
rows.note: go back to my hometown = pulang kampung / mudik

id.note: go back to my hometown = pulang kampung / mudik

blocks.text: **The Indonesian trap:** Indonesian has no past form. *Minggu lalu saya pergi ke pantai* uses the same *pergi* as today; only *minggu lalu* shows the past. English changes the verb too, in **every** sentence of your story: **Last weekend I went to the beach. We ate grilled fish and played volleyball.** Not *Last weekend I go to the beach…*, and not *I went to the beach and eat fish* (the second verb is past too). And the weekend is over, so **It was great**, not *It's great*.

id.text: **Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** bahasa Indonesia tidak punya bentuk lampau. *Minggu lalu saya pergi ke pantai* memakai *pergi* yang sama seperti hari ini; hanya *minggu lalu* yang menunjukkan masa lalu. Bahasa Inggris juga mengubah kata kerjanya, di **setiap** kalimat ceritamu: **Last weekend I went to the beach. We ate grilled fish and played volleyball.** Bukan *Last weekend I go to the beach…*, dan bukan *I went to the beach and eat fish* (kata kerja kedua juga lampau). Akhir pekannya juga sudah selesai, jadi **It was great**, bukan *It's great*.

blocks.prompt: On Monday Budi asks: 'What did you do on Saturday?' Choose the correct answer.
options: I go to the cinema with Dimas.
I went to the cinema with Dimas.
I'm going to the cinema with Dimas.
blocks.explain: Saturday is finished and Budi asks with did, so answer in the past: went. 'I go' is the Indonesian habit (no past form), and 'I'm going to the cinema' is a plan for later.

id.prompt: Hari Senin Budi bertanya: 'What did you do on Saturday?' Pilih jawaban yang benar.
id.explain: Hari Sabtu sudah lewat dan Budi bertanya dengan did, jadi jawab dengan bentuk lampau: went. 'I go' adalah kebiasaan dari bahasa Indonesia (tanpa bentuk lampau), dan 'I'm going to the cinema' adalah rencana untuk nanti.

blocks.text:
A one-word answer stops the chat. Add one or two **details**:
- **who**: *with my family, with friends from work, on my own* (= sendirian)
- **where**: *to Puncak, at a warung, in Bandung*
- **what it was like**: **It was** + an **adjective** (kata sifat: a word that describes something, like *fun, delicious*)

Join your ideas with **and**, **but** and **because**: *We went to Ancol, but it was very crowded. I stayed at home because I was tired.*

id.text:
Jawaban satu kata membuat obrolan berhenti. Tambahkan satu atau dua **detail**:
- **siapa**: *with my family, with friends from work, on my own* (= sendirian)
- **di mana**: *to Puncak, at a warung, in Bandung*
- **bagaimana rasanya**: **It was** + **adjective** (kata sifat: kata yang menggambarkan sesuatu, seperti *fun, delicious*)

Gabungkan idemu dengan **and**, **but**, dan **because**: *We went to Ancol, but it was very crowded. I stayed at home because I was tired.*

rows.note: macet = the traffic was bad / terrible

id.note: macet = the traffic was bad / terrible

blocks.text: **Two word traps.** *Seru* is **fun**, not *funny*: **funny** means lucu, something that makes you laugh, so *The trip was funny* sounds strange. And for feelings: **It was tiring** = the activity made you tired; **I was tired** = you were tired (saya capek). Both are correct, but *It was tired* is not.

id.text: **Dua jebakan kata.** *Seru* itu **fun**, bukan *funny*: **funny** artinya lucu, sesuatu yang bikin ketawa, jadi *The trip was funny* terdengar aneh. Lalu untuk perasaan: **It was tiring** = kegiatannya bikin capek; **I was tired** = kamu merasa capek (saya capek). Dua-duanya benar, tapi *It was tired* salah.

blocks.prompt: Sari asks: 'How was the concert?' You want to say 'Seru banget!'. Choose the correct answer.
blocks.explain: seru = fun (funny = lucu). The concert is finished, so was, not is.

id.prompt: Sari bertanya: 'How was the concert?' Kamu mau bilang 'Seru banget!'. Pilih jawaban yang benar.
id.explain: seru = fun (funny = lucu). Konsernya sudah selesai, jadi was, bukan is.

blocks.text:
On Friday the question moves to the future: **What are you going to do this weekend?** (= Akhir pekan ini mau ngapain?) or **What are you doing on Saturday?** (= Sabtu ada acara apa?). Answer with what you already know:
- your own plan → **I'm going to** + verb: *I'm going to visit my aunt in Bekasi.*
- something fixed with other people (a time, a ticket, a booking) → **I'm** + verb-**ing** + a time: *I'm meeting Sari at the cinema on Saturday at 7.*
- no plans → **Nothing special.** or **I'm not sure.**

Then add a detail, just like for the past: *I'm going to cook for my parents. It's my mother's birthday.*

id.text:
Hari Jumat pertanyaannya pindah ke masa depan: **What are you going to do this weekend?** (= Akhir pekan ini mau ngapain?) atau **What are you doing on Saturday?** (= Sabtu ada acara apa?). Jawab dengan yang sudah kamu tahu:
- rencanamu sendiri → **I'm going to** + kata kerja: *I'm going to visit my aunt in Bekasi.*
- acara yang sudah dijadwalkan dengan orang lain (ada jam, tiket, atau pesanan) → **I'm** + kata kerja-**ing** + waktu: *I'm meeting Sari at the cinema on Saturday at 7.*
- belum ada rencana → **Nothing special.** atau **I'm not sure.**

Lalu tambahkan detail, sama seperti untuk masa lalu: *I'm going to cook for my parents. It's my mother's birthday.*

rows.en: What are you going to do this weekend? — I'm going to visit my aunt in Bekasi.
rows.id: Akhir pekan ini mau ngapain? — Saya mau mengunjungi tante di Bekasi.

rows.en: What are you doing on Saturday? — I'm meeting Sari at the cinema at 7.
rows.id: Sabtu ada acara apa? — Saya ketemu Sari di bioskop jam 7.

rows.en: Nothing special. I'm going to relax at home.
rows.id: Nggak ada yang spesial. Saya mau santai di rumah.

rows.en: I'm going to Bandung on Sunday. My cousin is getting married.
rows.id: Hari Minggu saya ke Bandung. Sepupu saya menikah.
rows.note: going to + a place = pergi ke

blocks.text: **Listen to the question, then answer in the same time.** *What **did** you do?* → past (*I went…*). *What **are** you **going to** do?* / *What **are** you do**ing** on Saturday?* → future (*I'm going to… / I'm meeting…*). The Indonesian trap: *Besok saya ke Bogor* shows the future only with *besok*, so learners say *Tomorrow I go to Bogor*. Say **Tomorrow I'm going to Bogor** (or *I'm going to go to Bogor*).

id.text: **Dengarkan pertanyaannya, lalu jawab dengan waktu yang sama.** *What **did** you do?* → masa lalu (*I went…*). *What **are** you **going to** do?* / *What **are** you do**ing** on Saturday?* → masa depan (*I'm going to… / I'm meeting…*). Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: *Besok saya ke Bogor* menunjukkan masa depan hanya dengan *besok*, jadi pelajar bilang *Tomorrow I go to Bogor*. Katakan **Tomorrow I'm going to Bogor** (atau *I'm going to go to Bogor*).

blocks.prompt: It's Friday. Rina asks: 'What are you going to do this weekend?' Choose the correct answer.
options: I'm going to play futsal with my friends.
I play futsal with my friends.
I played futsal with my friends.
blocks.explain: Rina asks about a plan with going to, so answer with I'm going to + verb. 'I play' sounds like a habit, and 'I played' is the past: the weekend hasn't happened yet.

id.prompt: Hari Jumat. Rina bertanya: 'What are you going to do this weekend?' Pilih jawaban yang benar.
id.explain: Rina menanyakan rencana dengan going to, jadi jawab dengan I'm going to + kata kerja. 'I play' terdengar seperti kebiasaan, dan 'I played' itu masa lalu: akhir pekannya belum terjadi.

material.title: Follow-up questions: say a bit more

blocks.text:
After your first answer, people ask more: **Did you have a good time?** (= Seneng nggak?), **Was it expensive?** (= Mahal nggak?). A good answer has two parts: the **short answer** + **one more fact**.
- *Did you have a good time?* — **Yes, I did!** *We saw the sunset from the hill.*
- *Did you go alone?* — **No, I didn't.** *I went with my cousins.*
- *Was it expensive?* — **No, it wasn't.** *The hotel was only 300,000 rupiah a night.*

The short answer copies the **first word** of the question: **Did** → *I did / I didn't*; **Was** → *it was / it wasn't*. Just *Yes.* is correct, but then the conversation stops.

id.text:
Setelah jawaban pertamamu, orang biasanya bertanya lagi: **Did you have a good time?** (= Seneng nggak?), **Was it expensive?** (= Mahal nggak?). Jawaban yang bagus punya dua bagian: **jawaban singkat** + **satu fakta lagi**.
- *Did you have a good time?* — **Yes, I did!** *We saw the sunset from the hill.*
- *Did you go alone?* — **No, I didn't.** *I went with my cousins.*
- *Was it expensive?* — **No, it wasn't.** *The hotel was only 300,000 rupiah a night.*

Jawaban singkat mengikuti **kata pertama** pertanyaannya: **Did** → *I did / I didn't*; **Was** → *it was / it wasn't*. Jawab *Yes.* saja memang benar, tapi obrolannya jadi berhenti.

blocks.text: Don't answer a **did** question with *do* or *was*: *Did you like the food?* — **Yes, I did**, not *Yes, I do* or *Yes, I was*. And don't repeat the main verb in a short answer: *Did you see the fireworks?* — **Yes, I did**, not *Yes, I saw*.

id.text: Jangan jawab pertanyaan **did** dengan *do* atau *was*: *Did you like the food?* — **Yes, I did**, bukan *Yes, I do* atau *Yes, I was*. Dan jangan ulangi kata kerja utamanya di jawaban singkat: *Did you see the fireworks?* — **Yes, I did**, bukan *Yes, I saw*.

blocks.prompt: Dimas asks: 'Did you watch the match last night?' Choose the best answer.
options: Yes, I was. It was a great match.
Yes, I did! It was really exciting.
blocks.explain: A did question gets a did short answer: Yes, I did. One more fact keeps the chat going. 'I was' goes with Was questions, and 'Yes, I watch' repeats the verb in the present.

id.prompt: Dimas bertanya: 'Did you watch the match last night?' Pilih jawaban terbaik.
id.explain: Pertanyaan did dijawab singkat dengan did: Yes, I did. Satu fakta tambahan membuat obrolan terus berjalan. 'I was' untuk pertanyaan Was, dan 'Yes, I watch' mengulang kata kerja dalam bentuk sekarang.

id.title: Pertanyaan lanjutan: jawab sedikit lebih banyak

blocks.text:
A conversation goes both ways. After your answer, ask the other person: **And you?** / **How about you?** / **What about you?** (you know these), or a real follow-up question with **did**: **Where did you go? What did you eat? Was it fun?** Show interest with a short reaction: **Really? That's great! / Nice! / Oh no!**

**Word order:** question word + **did** + person + **base verb** (kata kerja dasar: the dictionary form, like *go, eat*): *Where **did** you **go**?*, not *Where you went?* or *Where did you went?* (did already shows the past). And when the Indonesian ends with *sama siapa*, English puts **with** at the end: *Kamu pergi sama siapa?* → **Who did you go with?**

id.text:
Percakapan itu dua arah. Setelah menjawab, tanya balik: **And you?** / **How about you?** / **What about you?** (kamu sudah tahu ini), atau pertanyaan lanjutan sungguhan dengan **did**: **Where did you go? What did you eat? Was it fun?** Tunjukkan minat dengan reaksi singkat: **Really? That's great! / Nice! / Oh no!**

**Urutan kata:** kata tanya + **did** + orang + **kata kerja dasar** (bentuk di kamus, seperti *go, eat*): *Where **did** you **go**?*, bukan *Where you went?* atau *Where did you went?* (did sudah menunjukkan masa lalu). Dan kalau bahasa Indonesianya berakhir dengan *sama siapa*, bahasa Inggris menaruh **with** di akhir: *Kamu pergi sama siapa?* → **Who did you go with?**

rows.en: Rina: How was your weekend, Budi?
Budi: Not bad, thanks. I went to my friend's wedding in Bogor. How about you?
rows.id: Budi: Lumayan, makasih. Saya ke pernikahan teman di Bogor. Kamu sendiri?

rows.en: Rina: I stayed at home because I was very tired. Was the food good?
rows.id: Rina: Saya di rumah aja karena capek banget. Makanannya enak?

rows.en: Budi: Yes, it was! I ate too much. What are you going to do next weekend?
rows.id: Budi: Enak! Saya kebanyakan makan. Akhir pekan depan mau ngapain?

rows.en: Rina: I'm going to visit my parents in Cirebon.
rows.id: Rina: Saya mau mengunjungi orang tua di Cirebon.

blocks.text: **The three-part answer:** 1) answer (*It was great!*), 2) add a detail (*I went to Bogor with my family*), 3) ask back (*How about you?*). Practise it out loud with your own weekend.

id.text: **Jawaban tiga bagian:** 1) jawab (*It was great!*), 2) tambahkan detail (*I went to Bogor with my family*), 3) tanya balik (*How about you?*). Latih dengan suara keras memakai cerita akhir pekanmu sendiri.

blocks.prompt: Sari says: 'I went to Surabaya last week.' Which follow-up question is correct?
blocks.explain: Question word + did + you + base verb: What did you do there? 'Who you went with?' has no did (Indonesian word order), and 'did you did' shows the past twice.

id.prompt: Sari bilang: 'I went to Surabaya last week.' Pertanyaan lanjutan mana yang benar?
id.explain: Kata tanya + did + you + kata kerja dasar: What did you do there? 'Who you went with?' tidak punya did (urutan kata bahasa Indonesia), dan 'did you did' menunjukkan masa lalu dua kali.

suggestedQuestions: What's the difference between 'How was your weekend?' and 'What did you do?'?
Is it OK to just answer 'Yes, I did'?
When do I say 'I'm going to…' and when 'I'm meeting…'?
How do I say 'pulang kampung' in English?

resources.title: Showing interest (A2 speaking)
resources.note: A short video chat where someone tells a story about their past, with phrases to react and show interest, plus practice tasks. The last discussion question uses a form you learn later (Have you ever…?).

id.note: Video obrolan pendek: seseorang menceritakan masa lalunya, dengan ungkapan untuk bereaksi dan menunjukkan minat, plus latihan. Pertanyaan diskusi terakhir memakai bentuk yang baru kamu pelajari nanti (Have you ever…?).

resources.title: Past tense: Lesson 23 (four short conversations)
resources.note: Listen to four short conversations about what people did yesterday and at the weekend, with the script and a quiz. Labelled A1, but it uses the same past simple and did questions as this lesson.

id.note: Dengarkan empat percakapan pendek tentang apa yang orang lakukan kemarin dan di akhir pekan, lengkap dengan teks dan kuis. Labelnya A1, tapi memakai past simple dan pertanyaan did yang sama dengan pelajaran ini.

flashcards.back: What are you going to do this weekend?
Did you have a good time? — Yes, I did!

id.intro: Hai! Hari Senin teman kantor bertanya 'How was your weekend?', dan hari Jumat 'What are you going to do this weekend?'. Di pelajaran ini kamu menggabungkan past simple dan going to untuk menjawab seperti di percakapan sungguhan: menceritakan apa yang kamu lakukan, menambah detail, menyampaikan rencana, dan bertanya balik. Pemanasan: how was your weekend?
suggestedQuestions: Apa bedanya 'How was your weekend?' dan 'What did you do?'?
Boleh nggak jawab 'Yes, I did' saja?
Kapan bilang 'I'm going to…' dan kapan 'I'm meeting…'?

assessment.spp-1: Hari Senin Pak Hasan bertanya: 'What did you do on Sunday?' Hari Minggumu: pergi ke mal bersama saudara perempuanmu (go to the mall with your sister). Jawab dalam satu kalimat bahasa Inggris.
assessment.spp-2: Dengarkan pertanyaan rekan kerjamu. Jawab dalam bahasa Inggris, satu atau dua kalimat pendek. Faktanya: seru (great) · pergi ke Lombok (go to Lombok).
assessment.spp-3: Hari Jumat. Temanmu bertanya: 'What are you going to do this weekend?' Rencanamu: membersihkan kamar (clean your room). Jawab dengan going to.
assessment.spp-4: Hari Sabtu kamu makan malam dengan Pak Hasan: dia sudah memesan meja untuk jam 7. Rina bertanya: 'What are you doing on Saturday?' Jawab dengan present continuous dari 'have'.
assessment.spp-5: Sari bertanya: 'Did you have a good time at the beach?' Jawab 'ya' dengan jawaban singkat, lalu tambahkan satu detail dalam bahasa Inggris. Detailnya: mengambil banyak foto (take a lot of photos).
assessment.spp-6: Temanmu Dimas bilang: 'I went to Bali last month.' Tanyakan pertanyaan lanjutan dalam bahasa Inggris dengan Where dan kata kerja 'stay' (menginap).
assessment.spp-7: Dengarkan temanmu. Jawab pertanyaannya dalam satu kalimat bahasa Inggris. Akhir pekanmu: di rumah saja dan menonton TV (stay at home and watch TV).
